definitions.gloss: soldier; common soldier; troops; the rank-and-file
definitions.explanation: A member of the armed forces, especially an ordinary soldier rather than an officer. Also used collectively for troops, and as the lowest grade in a military rank system.

examples.japanese: ⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧{兵|へい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すく}ない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧。
examples.english: There are few soldiers guarding the castle.

examples.japanese: ⟦{将軍|しょうぐん}→将軍：12386_shougun⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一万|いちまん}→一万：27599_ichiman⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{兵|へい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{率|ひき}いて→率いる：10879_hikiiru⟧⟦{進|すす}んだ→進む：01225_susumu⟧。
examples.english: The general advanced leading ten thousand soldiers.

notes:
A general word for a soldier or troops, common in historical and military contexts. As a single character it often feels formal or literary; everyday speech tends to use the compounds below.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {兵|へい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}る→送る：00742_okuru⟧: to send troops
- {兵|へい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{率|ひき}いる→率いる：10879_hikiiru⟧: to lead soldiers
- {兵|へい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{挙|あ}げる→挙げる：27889_ageru⟧: to raise an army

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{兵士|へいし}→兵士：11680_heishi⟧: soldier — the ordinary word for an individual serviceman
- ⟦{兵隊|へいたい}→兵隊：27666_heitai⟧: soldier; the troops — more colloquial, can mean a soldier or soldiers collectively
- ⟦{軍|ぐん}→軍：02677_gun⟧: army; military — the organization as a whole
